title: The Last Hollow
premise: Quentin Ashgrove, a bone-carver who hears the dead, keeps ledgers for the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things across the veil between realms. When a dying courier presses a map of the broken covenant into his hands, Quentin learns the guild's masters have been feeding on the dying boundary between worlds — and that they will kill to keep it that way. Hunted by his own employers and guided by the ghost of the courier and a disgraced covenant-warden named Sera Ilvane, Quentin must gather the scattered keystones of the old pact and reforge it at the Last Hollow, the place where the realms first touched. In the climax he discovers the covenant demands a living anchor willing to stay behind; Quentin offers himself, but Sera breaks the ledger's binding instead, splitting the cost between them. The covenant is reforged imperfectly but honestly, the guild's corrupt masters are unmade by their own debts, and Quentin and Sera walk out of the Hollow together — changed, diminished, and finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: Emrys Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and claims to have bought one haunted ledger too many. They write fantasy about paperwork, ghosts, and the people caught between them from a drafty house in the north of England.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In the guildhouse of Vellum & Ash, Quentin balances ledgers of impossible trades while the dead murmur through the bones he carves. He notices an entry erased by someone above him — a trade in 'boundary-toll.' The beat is quiet unease: a man who trusts systems discovering the system lies.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A bleeding courier collapses into the guildhouse at closing, pressing a bone map into Quentin's hands and whispering 'the Hollow remembers' before dying. The dead around Quentin suddenly go silent — then all speak at once. Beat: terror and reluctant responsibility as Quentin hides the map instead of surrendering it.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Owe
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Guildmaster Corvane questions Quentin gently, too gently, about the courier. Quentin lies for the first time in his careful life and feels the ledger-world tilt. He deciphers the map's first mark: a keystone beneath the drowned chapel of Lowmere. Beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Warden in Chains
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sera Ilvane, a covenant-warden imprisoned for refusing to falsify boundary reports, is released by Corvane — not freed, but assigned to hunt the map-thief. She recognizes the courier's name among her old case files. Beat: bitter pragmatism masking grief; she accepts the hunt to reach the truth first.

chapters.title: Lowmere Rising
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Fleeing the city by barge, Quentin reaches the drowned chapel and raises the first keystone with the courier's ghost coaching him from the bone in his pocket. The water recedes unnaturally far — something below noticed. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as he realizes the keystones are waking things up.

chapters.title: Two Thieves on One Road
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Sera corners Quentin at a crossroads inn; instead of arresting him, she reads the map and goes pale — she has seen its twin in the guild vaults. Uneasy alliance struck over bad wine. Beat: grudging respect; two lonely professionals recognizing each other's competence.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. To learn what the guild trades in boundary-toll, they infiltrate the Nightfair, where memories, years, and names are sold. Quentin finds vials labeled with the courier's stolen death-moments. Beat: moral horror — Quentin understands his ledgers priced human souls all along.

chapters.title: Sera's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Sera. By firelight, Sera admits she once signed off on a boundary 'adjustment' that let a village slip halfway out of the world; she was demoted, not punished, because she obeyed. Beat: shame offered like a wound; Quentin, keeper of debts, tells her some entries can only be rewritten, not paid.

chapters.title: The Second Keystone
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In the ash-fields of Karrek, they take the second keystone from a shrine guarded by guild bone-hounds. Sera fights magnificently and is wounded; Quentin hears the hounds' dead handlers begging forgiveness through their remains. Beat: victory with a price; the bond between the pair deepens under blood and smoke.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Summoned before Corvane, Sera is offered full reinstatement if she delivers Quentin and the map. He reveals the guild's creed: the covenant starves the strong realm to feed the weak, and the guild merely harvests the surplus. Beat: temptation framed as reason; Sera says nothing, and her silence damns her.

chapters.title: Ghost Country
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Crossing the thin place where the village slipped out of the world, Quentin walks among the half-gone living and the fully stranded dead. The courier's ghost begins to fade — the map is consuming its maker. Beat: tenderness and urgency; Quentin promises to finish what the courier started.

chapters.title: The Third Keystone Betrayed
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The third keystone rests in the guild's own vault. Sera leads Quentin in through her old credentials, but a fellow warden recognizes her and raises the alarm. They escape with the stone and a burning vault behind them. Beat: betrayal of her past self; Sera burns her old life literally and chooses Quentin's cause.

chapters.title: Interlude: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: POV Quentin, quiet chapter. Camped in ruins, Quentin carves a bone token for each dead voice that has helped them, giving the courier's ghost a body for one night. The ghost describes the Last Hollow and the covenant's original terms. Beat: elegy and clarity; the stakes become personal, not abstract.

chapters.title: The Toll Collectors
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Guild enforcers ambush them at the river ford; Sera is captured buying Quentin time to run with three keystones. Quentin faces his first true choice: flee to safety or turn back. Beat: love against duty made literal — he turns back, and gets captured too.

chapters.title: Chains and Conversations
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In Corvane's cells, Sera and Quentin are separated by a wall and talk through the stone. Corvane visits Quentin with the fourth keystone already in guild hands, offering partnership: reforge the covenant with the guild as its anchor-brokers. Beat: despair and intimacy through a wall; Quentin pretends to consider.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Corvane
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Using his bone-hearing on the cell wall's old mortar, Quentin uncovers the prison's buried records: Corvane has been skimming boundary-toll for decades and owes the covenant a debt it can collect. Beat: turning point — the enemy's power is built on an entry Quentin knows how to call due.

chapters.title: Escape by Entry
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Quentin invokes the covenant's collection clause aloud; the prison itself enforces the debt, doors unlocking, wards failing. They free other prisoners, including Sera's old accuser, and steal back the fourth keystone. Beat: exhilaration — the system Quentin served becomes the weapon against its master.

chapters.title: The Road to the Last Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Pursued across the moors, the fugitives race Corvane's remaining forces to the Hollow, where the courier's map shows the fifth keystone is not an object but a person: the last living anchor, hidden for generations. Beat: dread and resolve; the map's final line names a candidate — Quentin himself, born on the boundary.

chapters.title: The Hollow Opens
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At the Last Hollow, the veil hangs torn and howling. Quentin takes the anchor's position as the covenant reforges around him; he sees both realms whole and understands why anchors break — no one should hold that much belonging alone. Beat: transcendence and sacrifice; he prepares to stay forever.

chapters.title: The Broken Clause
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Corvane arrives to seize the reforging, but Sera invokes his unpaid toll before the covenant itself; the boundary collects, unmaking him into the ledger he lived by. Then Sera does the forbidden thing: she splits the anchor's burden, binding herself beside Quentin. Beat: climax of love against duty — she refuses a covenant that costs one person everything.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Two
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The covenant settles, imperfect and alive, anchored jointly. The realms stabilize; the dead of the Hollow cross over peacefully, the courier among them, thanking Quentin. The guild's honest remnant pledges to keep the new terms openly. Beat: exhaustion, grief, and grace; the impossible thing traded here was loneliness.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: POV Quentin, epilogue. Months later, Quentin and Sera run a small, transparent brokerage at the Hollow's edge, keeping a public ledger of what crosses and what it costs. Quentin still hears the dead, but now they mostly say thank you. Final beat: belonging — home is not a place you're given but a debt you choose to keep paying, together.
